questions.question: What are class methods in Ruby?
questions.title: Class Methods in Ruby
questions.direct_answer: A class method is called on the class itself, not an instance: `Greeter.hello` (not `Greeter.new.hello`). Define with `def self.name` or `def ClassName.name`: class Greeter; def self.hello; 'hi'; end; end; Greeter.hello # 'hi'. Class methods live on the class's singleton class — every class is itself an object, and class methods are its singleton methods. Use them for things that don't need instance state: factories (def self.from_json), utility helpers (Math.sqrt), counters (def self.count; @@count; end), config. They can't see instance variables (@x) — only class vars (@@x) and class-level state. `self` inside a class body refers to the class. To define many at once: `class << self; def a; end; def b; end; end` opens the singleton class. Instance methods = behavior of an instance; class methods = behavior of the class.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know class methods are called on the class (not an instance) and defined with `def self.name`.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Trying to call a class method on an instance (or vice versa), or accessing @x from a class method (only @@x works).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Class methods = called on the class (Greeter.hello); defined with def self.name or class << self. For factories, utilities, counters. Can't see @x.

sections.title: Class methods
sections.content:
```ruby
# Define a class method with `def self.name`
class Greeter
  def self.hello; 'hi from class'; end   # class method
  def hello;     'hi from instance'; end   # instance method
end

Greeter.hello            # 'hi from class'   (on the CLASS)
Greeter.new.hello       # 'hi from instance' (on an INSTANCE)
# Greeter.new.hello(class) -> NoMethodError

# Use cases (no instance state needed):
class User
  attr_accessor :name
  def initialize(name); @name = name; end

  # FACTORY: build an instance from data
  def self.from_json(json)
    new(JSON.parse(json)['name'])
  end

  # COUNTER: track how many were made
  @@count = 0
  def initialize(name); @name = name; @@count += 1; end
  def self.count; @@count; end
end
u = User.from_json('{"name":"Ada"}')   # factory
User.count                            # 1 (class-level counter)

# `self` inside class body = the class
class C
  puts self             # C
end

# Define many class methods: open the singleton class
class Math2
  class << self
    def square(x); x * x; end
    def cube(x);   x * x * x; end
  end
end
Math2.square(3)         # 9
Math2.cube(2)           # 8

# Class methods CANNOT see instance vars (@x) — only @@x / class state.
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Calling a class method on an instance (or vice versa) — NoMethodError.
Accessing @x (instance var) from a class method — only @@x is visible.
Forgetting `self` in def self.name (def name is an instance method).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: A class method is called on the class itself (Greeter.hello, not Greeter.new.hello).
Define with `def self.name` or open `class << self` for many.
Use for factories (from_json), utilities (Math.sqrt), counters (@@count), config.
Class methods can't see instance vars (@x) — only class vars (@@x) and class state.
`self` inside a class body refers to the class; class methods live on the singleton class.
